content.text:
The Write tool is not available in this context, so I'll deliver the plan directly as my response.

# Implementation plan: `intropy sys create`

## Verified ground truth (what the design rests on)

- `template.Create` (internal/template/create.go:71) already does: resolve tag → download tarball → `Resolve` values → render skeleton → process dependencies → `WriteScaffold` → optional `--output-json`. Reusing it gives step 3 and step 6 of the spec for free.
- `Resolve` (internal/template/values.go:34) renders `spec.values` derivations into the returned value map, and `Create` writes that map into the host's `.intropy/scaffold.json`. So **after** `template.Create` returns, the host's own scaffold record contains the template-derived `projectName`, `systemClass`, and `pubsub` values. This is the key design decision: **codegen learns the file/class names by reading back the just-written host scaffold record** (`template.LoadScaffold(filepath.Join(outputDir, template.ScaffoldRelPath))`), never by reimplementing the sprig expression `{{ .name | replace "-" " " | title | replace " " "" }}` in Go. sprig v3.3.0's `title` is deprecated `strings.Title` — reimplementing it is exactly the drift trap the template.yaml comment warns about; reading back the resolved values makes disagreement impossible.
- sprig v3.3.0 `kebabcase` **is** `xstrings.ToKebabCase` (verified in sprig functions.go:148), and `github.com/huandu/xstrings v1.5.0` is already in go.mod (indirect). Calling `xstrings.ToKebabCase` from the CLI gives exact parity with the templates' `{{ .name | kebabcase }}`; it just moves to the direct `require` block. It's also idempotent on already-kebab input (`order-flow` → `order-flow`).
- `template.ListScaffolds` (scaffold_list.go:36) returns `[]ScaffoldEntry{Path, Scaffold}` + warnings, skips `.git`/`.intropy`/`bin`/`dist`/`node_modules`, and does not descend into matched project roots.
- extractor/loader template.yaml already carry labels `intropy.dev/block-kind` + `intropy.dev/data-flow`, and values `appId` (derived) and `topic` (parameter). They do **not** yet emit `contract` or `pubsub` values — that's the companion change. shared-models carries `intropy.dev/template-role: shared-library`, parameter `name` (conventionally `Models`), namespace = `{{ .name }}`, csproj file = `{{ .name }}.csproj`.
- The rendered host csproj (skeleton/`{{ .projectName }}.SystemHost.csproj.tmpl`) is plain hand-formatted XML with a single closing `</Project>` and an existing `Exists`-guarded `<ProjectName>.Contracts` reference that the tutorial has obsoleted.

---

## Step 0 (prerequisite, own commit): record block-kind/data-flow in scaffold.json

**Modify `internal/template/scaffold.go`**
- Add constants:
  ```go
  TemplateBlockKindLabel = "intropy.dev/block-kind"
  TemplateDataFlowLabel  = "intropy.dev/data-flow"
  BlockKindExtractor = "extractor"
  BlockKindLoader    = "loader"
  ```
- Add fields to `Scaffold` (additive, no schemaVersion bump — the struct comment at line 14 explicitly permits this):
  ```go
  BlockKind string `json:"blockKind,omitempty"` // intropy.dev/block-kind label
  DataFlow  string `json:"dataFlow,omitempty"`  // intropy.dev/data-flow label
  ```
- Helpers next to `roleFromLabels`: `blockKindFromLabels`, `dataFlowFromLabels` (or one `labelValue(labels, key)`).

**Modify both writers** (mirror the existing `Role:` line):
- `internal/template/create.go:116` — add `BlockKind: blockKindFromLabels(tmpl.Metadata.Labels), DataFlow: dataFlowFromLabels(...)`.
- `internal/template/dependencies.go:132` — same for dependency renders.

**Tests**: extend `TestCreateWritesScaffoldFile` (create_test.go) with a template YAML variant carrying the labels; assert the record round-trips both fields. One analogous assertion in dependencies_test.go.

---

## Step 1: new package `internal/system` — model + classify/validate (pure, no I/O)

New file **`internal/system/model.go`**:

```go
package system

type TopicKey struct {
    Pubsub string `json:"pubsub"`
    Name   string `json:"topic"`
}

type Topic struct {
    TopicKey
    Contract string `json:"contract"` // C# type name from values.contract
    Field    string `json:"-"`        // PascalCase field name in Topics.cs, e.g. Orders
}

type Component struct {
    AppID string   `json:"name"` // values.appId; the AddExtractor/AddLoader argument
    Kind  string   `json:"kind"` // template.BlockKindExtractor | BlockKindLoader
    Topic TopicKey `json:"-"`
    Path  string   `json:"path"` // scaffold dir as reported by ListScaffolds (error messages)
}

type SharedLibrary struct {
    Path string // scaffold dir
    Name string // values.name, e.g. "Models" — namespace AND csproj basename
}

type Model struct {
    Name        string // kebab system name
    ProjectName string // filled from host scaffold record after render
    SystemClass string // filled from host scaffold record after render
    Components  []Component
    Topics      []Topic // sorted by (Pubsub, Name)
    Shared      SharedLibrary
}
```

New file **`internal/system/assemble.go`** — the scan/classify/validate algorithm:

```go
// Assemble classifies workspace scaffold records into a system model.
// warnf receives skip warnings; the returned model has Name/ProjectName/
// SystemClass unset (the caller fills them around the template render).
func Assemble(entries []template.ScaffoldEntry, warnf func(format string, args ...any)) (*Model, error)
```

Algorithm (exact order):
1. Partition entries:
   - `Role == template.RoleSharedLibrary` → shared-library candidates.
   - `Role == "system-host"` → skip silently-ish: `warnf("skipping %s: an existing system host (re-run with --force writes into its directory)", e.Path)` — this keeps `--force` re-runs working, since the previous run's own record is in the walk.
   - `BlockKind` is `extractor`/`loader` → component candidates.
   - `BlockKind` set but other value → `warnf("skipping %s: unsupported block kind %q (sys create assembles extractors and loaders only)", e.Path, kind)`.
   - Neither role nor blockKind → `warnf("skipping %s: scaffold record has no block kind — re-scaffold with a newer template release to include it", e.Path)`.
2. For each component candidate, extract typed values with a helper that handles the JSON `map[string]any` trap:
   ```go
   // stringValue returns values[key] as a non-empty string, with errors that
   // name the record: "orders-extractor/.intropy/scaffold.json: values.contract
   // is missing" / "... has type float64, expected string".
   func stringValue(e template.ScaffoldEntry, key string) (string, error)
   ```
   Required: `appId`, `topic`, `contract`. Optional: `pubsub` via `stringValueDefault(e, "pubsub", "pubsub")` — default `"pubsub"` matches both the extractor skeleton's `PubSubName = "pubsub"` constant and the system-host template value, so pre-companion-change records still assemble. Missing `contract` gets a guidance suffix: `re-scaffold this integration with a template release that records the contract type, or add "contract": "<TypeName>" to the record's values`.
3. Validate:
   - **Zero components** → sentinel error:
     ```go
     var ErrNoComponents = errors.New("no assemblable integration scaffolds found")
     ```
     wrapped with guidance: `scaffold extractors/loaders first ('intropy int create extractor -n ... -s topic=...'), then run 'intropy sys create' from the workspace root`.
   - **Duplicate appId** → `duplicate component name %q: declared by both %s and %s (component names must be unique in a system)`.
   - **Contract conflict**: group by `TopicKey`; conflicting `contract` → `topic %q on pubsub %q has conflicting contracts: %q (%s) vs %q (%s)`.
   - **Shared library — zero** → error (decision: error, the tutorial guarantees `Models/` exists via the extractor/loader `spec.dependencies`): `no shared contracts project found (template role %q): Topics.cs needs the contract types; components scaffolded from the official extractor/loader templates create a sibling Models/ project automatically`.
   - **Shared library — multiple** → error (decision: error, not pick+warn — the `using` and ProjectReference would be ambiguous): `found %d shared contract projects (%s); a system host references exactly one — remove or consolidate before re-running`.
   - **Topic field collision** (edge case: `order-events` vs `order.events` both PascalCase to `OrderEvents`): error naming both topics.
4. Build `Topics` sorted by `(Pubsub, Name)`; `Field = pascalIdent(topic)`. Components keep `ListScaffolds` walk order (lexical, deterministic).

```go
// pascalIdent converts a DNS-ish topic name to a C# identifier: split on
// '-' and '.', upper-case each segment's first rune ("order-events" → "OrderEvents").
func pascalIdent(s string) string
```

## Step 2: codegen — `internal/system/codegen.go`

**Decision: embedded `text/template` const strings** (not `fmt.Fprintf` chains, not go:embed — two small files don't justify separate assets; `text/template` keeps the C# shape readable and diffable in one place). Plain `template.New(...).Parse(topicsTmpl)` at package init, no sprig needed. Output matches the tutorial exactly, including **no C# namespace** (the tutorial files are namespace-less; the placeholders' `namespace {{ .projectName }}.SystemHost;` gets overwritten — flagged as an inconsistency below).

```go
func writeTopicsFile(dir string, m *Model) error       // overwrites <dir>/Topics.cs
func writeSystemClassFile(dir string, m *Model) error  // overwrites <dir>/<SystemClass>.cs
```

`Topics.cs` shape (per topic; `using Models;` comes from `m.Shared.Name`):

```csharp
using Intropy.Topology;
using Models;

/// <summary>The system's topics, each defined once and shared by every component that touches it.</summary>
public static class Topics
{
    /// <summary>Order messages on topic 'orders' (pubsub 'pubsub').</summary>
    public static readonly TopicRef<Order> Orders = TopicRef<Order>.Define("pubsub", "orders");
}
```

(Per-topic doc summary is generated generically — `{{ .Contract }} messages on topic '{{ .Name }}' (pubsub '{{ .Pubsub }}').` — the tutorial's richer prose ("flowing from the extractor to the loader") is human-written; don't fake it.)

`<SystemClass>.cs` shape:

```csharp
using Intropy.Topology;

/// <summary>The order-flow system: what exists, and what connects it.</summary>
public sealed class OrderFlowSystem : ISystemDefinition
{
    public string SystemName => "order-flow";

    public void Define(SystemBuilder builder)
    {
        builder.AddExtractor("order-extractor").Publishes(Topics.Orders);
        builder.AddLoader("order-loader").Subscribes(Topics.Orders);
    }
}
```

Per component: `AddExtractor` + `.Publishes(Topics.<Field>)` for kind extractor, `AddLoader` + `.Subscribes(Topics.<Field>)` for loader; the `<Field>` is looked up from the component's `TopicKey`.

Both writes go through the existing `writeAtomically` pattern — simplest: `os.WriteFile` is fine here since the directory is freshly rendered, but reuse of a small atomic write keeps parity; decide at implementation time (non-load-bearing).

**Safety check before writing**: stat `<dir>/<SystemClass>.cs`. If it does not exist, fail with `template rendered no %s.cs placeholder — the template's systemClass derivation disagrees with this CLI (template %s@%s); upgrade intropy or the template` rather than silently adding a second `ISystemDefinition` (the exact failure mode the template.yaml comment warns about).

---

## Step 3: csproj insertion — `internal/system/csproj.go`

**Decision: string insertion before the final `</Project>`, not `encoding/xml`.** Rationale verified against the actual rendered csproj: it is hand-formatted MSBuild XML with comments, attribute-heavy self-closing elements, and 4-space indentation. `encoding/xml` round-tripping destroys comments/formatting and mangles self-closing tags; every dotnet-adjacent tool (dotnet CLI itself included) edits csproj textually or via MSBuild APIs we don't have. The file was rendered by us seconds earlier, so its shape is fully known.

```go
// insertProjectReference inserts an ItemGroup with a ProjectReference to the
// shared contracts project immediately before the closing </Project> tag.
// include is slash-separated and relative to the csproj's directory.
func insertProjectReference(csprojPath, include string) error
```

- Read file; `idx := strings.LastIndex(content, "</Project>")`; if `idx < 0` → `rendered %s has no </Project> closing tag` error.
- Insert:
  ```
      <ItemGroup>
          <!-- Shared contracts project, referenced by `intropy sys create`. -->
          <ProjectReference Include="../Models/Models.csproj" IsAspireProjectResource="false" />
      </ItemGroup>

  ```
  `IsAspireProjectResource="false"` is required — the skeleton's own (to-be-removed) Contracts reference sets it, because an Aspire AppHost otherwise treats every `ProjectReference` as an Aspire resource.
- The `Include` path: `rel, _ := filepath.Rel(absOutputDir, absSharedPath)` → `path.Join(filepath.ToSlash(rel), shared.Name + ".csproj")` → e.g. `../Models/Models.csproj`. Error if `filepath.Rel` fails (different volumes on Windows).

## Step 4: orchestration — `internal/system/create.go`

```go
type CreateOptions struct {
    Name       string // -n as typed; PascalCase or kebab
    StartDir   string // workspace scan root; default "."
    OutputDir  string // default: kebab-cased Name
    Version    string // template release tag; default latest
    Force      bool
    OutputJSON string // "-" for stdout
    Stdout     io.Writer
    Stderr     io.Writer
    HTTP       *http.Client
    UserAgent  string

    // Test overrides, zero-valued in production (same seam as template/deploy).
    Owner, Repo, GitHubBaseURL string
}

// CreateResult mirrors template.CreateResult plus the assembled system.
type CreateResult struct {
    Template  string         `json:"template"` // "system-host"
    Owner     string         `json:"owner"`
    Repo      string         `json:"repo"`
    Version   string         `json:"version"`
    OutputDir string         `json:"outputDir"`
    Values    map[string]any `json:"values"`
    System    SystemSummary  `json:"system"`
}

type SystemSummary struct { // loosely mirrors `dotnet run -- graph`
    Name          string      `json:"name"`
    Components    []Component `json:"components"`
    Topics        []Topic     `json:"topics"`
    SharedLibrary string      `json:"sharedLibrary"` // scaffold dir path
}

func Create(ctx context.Context, opts CreateOptions) error
```

Exact sequence inside `Create` (fail-fast ordering: all local validation before any network I/O):

1. `applyDefaults()`; `kebab := xstrings.ToKebabCase(opts.Name)`; if `opts.OutputDir == ""` → `opts.OutputDir = kebab`. (Name-format errors beyond that are caught by the template's DNS-1123 `pattern` during `Resolve` — same behavior as `int create`, no duplicated regex in the CLI.)
2. `entries, warnings := template.ListScaffolds(opts.StartDir)`; print each warning to `Stderr` prefixed `warning:`.
3. `model, err := Assemble(entries, warnf)` — all classification/validation errors surface here, before any GitHub call.
4. Compute the csproj `Include` path from `opts.OutputDir` ↔ `model.Shared.Path` (fails early on pathological layouts).
5. Render the host:
   ```go
   template.Create(ctx, template.CreateOptions{
       Template:  "system-host",
       OutputDir: opts.OutputDir,
       Version:   opts.Version,
       SetValues: map[string]any{"name": kebab},
       Force:     opts.Force,
       NoInput:   true,               // template contract: only `name`, never prompt
       Stdin:     strings.NewReader(""),
       Stdout: opts.Stdout, Stderr: opts.Stderr,
       HTTP: opts.HTTP, UserAgent: opts.UserAgent,
       Owner: opts.Owner, Repo: opts.Repo, GitHubBaseURL: opts.GitHubBaseURL,
       // OutputJSON deliberately NOT forwarded — sys create writes its own richer result.
   })
   ```
   This also writes the host's scaffold record (spec step 6) with `Role: "system-host"` — free via the Step 0/existing machinery. `--force` semantics (non-empty dir refusal) come from `ensureOutputDir` unchanged.
6. Read back: `rec, err := template.LoadScaffold(filepath.Join(opts.OutputDir, filepath.FromSlash(template.ScaffoldRelPath)))`; extract `projectName`, `systemClass` as strings (via the same `stringValue`-style guard); error `template %s@%s did not derive projectName/systemClass values` if absent. Set `model.Name = kebab`, `model.ProjectName`, `model.SystemClass`.
7. Placeholder existence check (Step 2 safety check) → `writeTopicsFile` → `writeSystemClassFile`.
8. `insertProjectReference(filepath.Join(opts.OutputDir, projectName+".SystemHost.csproj"), include)` — error if the csproj file is missing.
9. Summary to `Stderr`: `assembled system 'order-flow': 2 components, 1 topic, contracts from Models/` and `created <outputDir>` (the `template.Create` fetch/create lines already appeared).
10. `maybeWriteCreateResult` (same shape as deploy/create.go:188 — factor or copy the small stdout-vs-file writer).

The Write tool is not available in this context, so I'll deliver the plan directly as my response.

# Implementation plan: `intropy sys create`

## Verified ground truth (what the design rests on)

- `template.Create` (internal/template/create.go:71) already does: resolve tag → download tarball → `Resolve` values → render skeleton → process dependencies → `WriteScaffold` → optional `--output-json`. Reusing it gives step 3 and step 6 of the spec for free.
- `Resolve` (internal/template/values.go:34) renders `spec.values` derivations into the returned value map, and `Create` writes that map into the host's `.intropy/scaffold.json`. So **after** `template.Create` returns, the host's own scaffold record contains the template-derived `projectName`, `systemClass`, and `pubsub` values. This is the key design decision: **codegen learns the file/class names by reading back the just-written host scaffold record** (`template.LoadScaffold(filepath.Join(outputDir, template.ScaffoldRelPath))`), never by reimplementing the sprig expression `{{ .name | replace "-" " " | title | replace " " "" }}` in Go. sprig v3.3.0's `title` is deprecated `strings.Title` — reimplementing it is exactly the drift trap the template.yaml comment warns about; reading back the resolved values makes disagreement impossible.
- sprig v3.3.0 `kebabcase` **is** `xstrings.ToKebabCase` (verified in sprig functions.go:148), and `github.com/huandu/xstrings v1.5.0` is already in go.mod (indirect). Calling `xstrings.ToKebabCase` from the CLI gives exact parity with the templates' `{{ .name | kebabcase }}`; it just moves to the direct `require` block. It's also idempotent on already-kebab input (`order-flow` → `order-flow`).
- `template.ListScaffolds` (scaffold_list.go:36) returns `[]ScaffoldEntry{Path, Scaffold}` + warnings, skips `.git`/`.intropy`/`bin`/`dist`/`node_modules`, and does not descend into matched project roots.
- extractor/loader template.yaml already carry labels `intropy.dev/block-kind` + `intropy.dev/data-flow`, and values `appId` (derived) and `topic` (parameter). They do **not** yet emit `contract` or `pubsub` values — that's the companion change. shared-models carries `intropy.dev/template-role: shared-library`, parameter `name` (conventionally `Models`), namespace = `{{ .name }}`, csproj file = `{{ .name }}.csproj`.
- The rendered host csproj (skeleton/`{{ .projectName }}.SystemHost.csproj.tmpl`) is plain hand-formatted XML with a single closing `</Project>` and an existing `Exists`-guarded `<ProjectName>.Contracts` reference that the tutorial has obsoleted.

---

## Step 0 (prerequisite, own commit): record block-kind/data-flow in scaffold.json

**Modify `internal/template/scaffold.go`**
- Add constants:
  ```go
  TemplateBlockKindLabel = "intropy.dev/block-kind"
  TemplateDataFlowLabel  = "intropy.dev/data-flow"
  BlockKindExtractor = "extractor"
  BlockKindLoader    = "loader"
  ```
- Add fields to `Scaffold` (additive, no schemaVersion bump — the struct comment at line 14 explicitly permits this):
  ```go
  BlockKind string `json:"blockKind,omitempty"` // intropy.dev/block-kind label
  DataFlow  string `json:"dataFlow,omitempty"`  // intropy.dev/data-flow label
  ```
- Helpers next to `roleFromLabels`: `blockKindFromLabels`, `dataFlowFromLabels` (or one `labelValue(labels, key)`).

**Modify both writers** (mirror the existing `Role:` line):
- `internal/template/create.go:116` — add `BlockKind: blockKindFromLabels(tmpl.Metadata.Labels), DataFlow: dataFlowFromLabels(...)`.
- `internal/template/dependencies.go:132` — same for dependency renders.

**Tests**: extend `TestCreateWritesScaffoldFile` (create_test.go) with a template YAML variant carrying the labels; assert the record round-trips both fields. One analogous assertion in dependencies_test.go.

---

## Step 1: new package `internal/system` — model + classify/validate (pure, no I/O)

New file **`internal/system/model.go`**:

```go
package system

type TopicKey struct {
    Pubsub string `json:"pubsub"`
    Name   string `json:"topic"`
}

type Topic struct {
    TopicKey
    Contract string `json:"contract"` // C# type name from values.contract
    Field    string `json:"-"`        // PascalCase field name in Topics.cs, e.g. Orders
}

type Component struct {
    AppID string   `json:"name"` // values.appId; the AddExtractor/AddLoader argument
    Kind  string   `json:"kind"` // template.BlockKindExtractor | BlockKindLoader
    Topic TopicKey `json:"-"`
    Path  string   `json:"path"` // scaffold dir as reported by ListScaffolds (error messages)
}

type SharedLibrary struct {
    Path string // scaffold dir
    Name string // values.name, e.g. "Models" — namespace AND csproj basename
}

type Model struct {
    Name        string // kebab system name
    ProjectName string // filled from host scaffold record after render
    SystemClass string // filled from host scaffold record after render
    Components  []Component
    Topics      []Topic // sorted by (Pubsub, Name)
    Shared      SharedLibrary
}
```

New file **`internal/system/assemble.go`** — the scan/classify/validate algorithm:

```go
// Assemble classifies workspace scaffold records into a system model.
// warnf receives skip warnings; the returned model has Name/ProjectName/
// SystemClass unset (the caller fills them around the template render).
func Assemble(entries []template.ScaffoldEntry, warnf func(format string, args ...any)) (*Model, error)
```

Algorithm (exact order):
1. Partition entries:
   - `Role == template.RoleSharedLibrary` → shared-library candidates.
   - `Role == "system-host"` → skip silently-ish: `warnf("skipping %s: an existing system host (re-run with --force writes into its directory)", e.Path)` — this keeps `--force` re-runs working, since the previous run's own record is in the walk.
   - `BlockKind` is `extractor`/`loader` → component candidates.
   - `BlockKind` set but other value → `warnf("skipping %s: unsupported block kind %q (sys create assembles extractors and loaders only)", e.Path, kind)`.
   - Neither role nor blockKind → `warnf("skipping %s: scaffold record has no block kind — re-scaffold with a newer template release to include it", e.Path)`.
2. For each component candidate, extract typed values with a helper that handles the JSON `map[string]any` trap:
   ```go
   // stringValue returns values[key] as a non-empty string, with errors that
   // name the record: "orders-extractor/.intropy/scaffold.json: values.contract
   // is missing" / "... has type float64, expected string".
   func stringValue(e template.ScaffoldEntry, key string) (string, error)
   ```
   Required: `appId`, `topic`, `contract`. Optional: `pubsub` via `stringValueDefault(e, "pubsub", "pubsub")` — default `"pubsub"` matches both the extractor skeleton's `PubSubName = "pubsub"` constant and the system-host template value, so pre-companion-change records still assemble. Missing `contract` gets a guidance suffix: `re-scaffold this integration with a template release that records the contract type, or add "contract": "<TypeName>" to the record's values`.
3. Validate:
   - **Zero components** → sentinel error:
     ```go
     var ErrNoComponents = errors.New("no assemblable integration scaffolds found")
     ```
     wrapped with guidance: `scaffold extractors/loaders first ('intropy int create extractor -n ... -s topic=...'), then run 'intropy sys create' from the workspace root`.
   - **Duplicate appId** → `duplicate component name %q: declared by both %s and %s (component names must be unique in a system)`.
   - **Contract conflict**: group by `TopicKey`; conflicting `contract` → `topic %q on pubsub %q has conflicting contracts: %q (%s) vs %q (%s)`.
   - **Shared library — zero** → error (decision: error, the tutorial guarantees `Models/` exists via the extractor/loader `spec.dependencies`): `no shared contracts project found (template role %q): Topics.cs needs the contract types; components scaffolded from the official extractor/loader templates create a sibling Models/ project automatically`.
   - **Shared library — multiple** → error (decision: error, not pick+warn — the `using` and ProjectReference would be ambiguous): `found %d shared contract projects (%s); a system host references exactly one — remove or consolidate before re-running`.
   - **Topic field collision** (edge case: `order-events` vs `order.events` both PascalCase to `OrderEvents`): error naming both topics.
4. Build `Topics` sorted by `(Pubsub, Name)`; `Field = pascalIdent(topic)`. Components keep `ListScaffolds` walk order (lexical, deterministic).

```go
// pascalIdent converts a DNS-ish topic name to a C# identifier: split on
// '-' and '.', upper-case each segment's first rune ("order-events" → "OrderEvents").
func pascalIdent(s string) string
```

---

## Step 2: codegen — `internal/system/codegen.go`

**Decision: embedded `text/template` const strings** (not `fmt.Fprintf` chains, not go:embed — two small files don't justify separate assets; `text/template` keeps the C# shape readable and diffable in one place). Plain `template.New(...).Parse(topicsTmpl)` at package init, no sprig needed. Output matches the tutorial exactly, including **no C# namespace** (the tutorial files are namespace-less; the placeholders' `namespace {{ .projectName }}.SystemHost;` gets overwritten — flagged as an inconsistency below).

```go
func writeTopicsFile(dir string, m *Model) error       // overwrites <dir>/Topics.cs
func writeSystemClassFile(dir string, m *Model) error  // overwrites <dir>/<SystemClass>.cs
```

`Topics.cs` shape (per topic; `using Models;` comes from `m.Shared.Name`):

```csharp
using Intropy.Topology;
using Models;

/// <summary>The system's topics, each defined once and shared by every component that touches it.</summary>
public static class Topics
{
    /// <summary>Order messages on topic 'orders' (pubsub 'pubsub').</summary>
    public static readonly TopicRef<Order> Orders = TopicRef<Order>.Define("pubsub", "orders");
}
```

(Per-topic doc summary is generated generically — `{{ .Contract }} messages on topic '{{ .Name }}' (pubsub '{{ .Pubsub }}').` — the tutorial's richer prose ("flowing from the extractor to the loader") is human-written; don't fake it.)

`<SystemClass>.cs` shape:

```csharp
using Intropy.Topology;

/// <summary>The order-flow system: what exists, and what connects it.</summary>
public sealed class OrderFlowSystem : ISystemDefinition
{
    public string SystemName => "order-flow";

    public void Define(SystemBuilder builder)
    {
        builder.AddExtractor("order-extractor").Publishes(Topics.Orders);
        builder.AddLoader("order-loader").Subscribes(Topics.Orders);
    }
}
```

Per component: `AddExtractor` + `.Publishes(Topics.<Field>)` for kind extractor, `AddLoader` + `.Subscribes(Topics.<Field>)` for loader; the `<Field>` is looked up from the component's `TopicKey`.

Both writes go through the existing `writeAtomically` pattern — simplest: `os.WriteFile` is fine here since the directory is freshly rendered, but reuse of a small atomic write keeps parity; decide at implementation time (non-load-bearing).

**Safety check before writing**: stat `<dir>/<SystemClass>.cs`. If it does not exist, fail with `template rendered no %s.cs placeholder — the template's systemClass derivation disagrees with this CLI (template %s@%s); upgrade intropy or the template` rather than silently adding a second `ISystemDefinition` (the exact failure mode the template.yaml comment warns about).

---

## Step 3: csproj insertion — `internal/system/csproj.go`

**Decision: string insertion before the final `</Project>`, not `encoding/xml`.** Rationale verified against the actual rendered csproj: it is hand-formatted MSBuild XML with comments, attribute-heavy self-closing elements, and 4-space indentation. `encoding/xml` round-tripping destroys comments/formatting and mangles self-closing tags; every dotnet-adjacent tool (dotnet CLI itself included) edits csproj textually or via MSBuild APIs we don't have. The file was rendered by us seconds earlier, so its shape is fully known.

```go
// insertProjectReference inserts an ItemGroup with a ProjectReference to the
// shared contracts project immediately before the closing </Project> tag.
// include is slash-separated and relative to the csproj's directory.
func insertProjectReference(csprojPath, include string) error
```

- Read file; `idx := strings.LastIndex(content, "</Project>")`; if `idx < 0` → `rendered %s has no </Project> closing tag` error.
- Insert:
  ```
      <ItemGroup>
          <!-- Shared contracts project, referenced by `intropy sys create`. -->
          <ProjectReference Include="../Models/Models.csproj" IsAspireProjectResource="false" />
      </ItemGroup>

  ```
  `IsAspireProjectResource="false"` is required — the skeleton's own (to-be-removed) Contracts reference sets it, because an Aspire AppHost otherwise treats every `ProjectReference` as an Aspire resource.
- The `Include` path: `rel, _ := filepath.Rel(absOutputDir, absSharedPath)` → `path.Join(filepath.ToSlash(rel), shared.Name + ".csproj")` → e.g. `../Models/Models.csproj`. Error if `filepath.Rel` fails (different volumes on Windows).

---

## Step 4: orchestration — `internal/system/create.go`

```go
type CreateOptions struct {
    Name       string // -n as typed; PascalCase or kebab
    StartDir   string // workspace scan root; default "."
    OutputDir  string // default: kebab-cased Name
    Version    string // template release tag; default latest
    Force      bool
    OutputJSON string // "-" for stdout
    Stdout     io.Writer
    Stderr     io.Writer
    HTTP       *http.Client
    UserAgent  string

    // Test overrides, zero-valued in production (same seam as template/deploy).
    Owner, Repo, GitHubBaseURL string
}

// CreateResult mirrors template.CreateResult plus the assembled system.
type CreateResult struct {
    Template  string         `json:"template"` // "system-host"
    Owner     string         `json:"owner"`
    Repo      string         `json:"repo"`
    Version   string         `json:"version"`
    OutputDir string         `json:"outputDir"`
    Values    map[string]any `json:"values"`
    System    SystemSummary  `json:"system"`
}

type SystemSummary struct { // loosely mirrors `dotnet run -- graph`
    Name          string      `json:"name"`
    Components    []Component `json:"components"`
    Topics        []Topic     `json:"topics"`
    SharedLibrary string      `json:"sharedLibrary"` // scaffold dir path
}

func Create(ctx context.Context, opts CreateOptions) error
```

Exact sequence inside `Create` (fail-fast ordering: all local validation before any network I/O):

1. `applyDefaults()`; `kebab := xstrings.ToKebabCase(opts.Name)`; if `opts.OutputDir == ""` → `opts.OutputDir = kebab`. (Name-format errors beyond that are caught by the template's DNS-1123 `pattern` during `Resolve` — same behavior as `int create`, no duplicated regex in the CLI.)
2. `entries, warnings := template.ListScaffolds(opts.StartDir)`; print each warning to `Stderr` prefixed `warning:`.
3. `model, err := Assemble(entries, warnf)` — all classification/validation errors surface here, before any GitHub call.
4. Compute the csproj `Include` path from `opts.OutputDir` ↔ `model.Shared.Path` (fails early on pathological layouts).
5. Render the host:
   ```go
   template.Create(ctx, template.CreateOptions{
       Template:  "system-host",
       OutputDir: opts.OutputDir,
       Version:   opts.Version,
       SetValues: map[string]any{"name": kebab},
       Force:     opts.Force,
       NoInput:   true,               // template contract: only `name`, never prompt
       Stdin:     strings.NewReader(""),
       Stdout: opts.Stdout, Stderr: opts.Stderr,
       HTTP: opts.HTTP, UserAgent: opts.UserAgent,
       Owner: opts.Owner, Repo: opts.Repo, GitHubBaseURL: opts.GitHubBaseURL,
       // OutputJSON deliberately NOT forwarded — sys create writes its own richer result.
   })
   ```
   This also writes the host's scaffold record (spec step 6) with `Role: "system-host"` — free via the Step 0/existing machinery. `--force` semantics (non-empty dir refusal) come from `ensureOutputDir` unchanged.
6. Read back: `rec, err := template.LoadScaffold(filepath.Join(opts.OutputDir, filepath.FromSlash(template.ScaffoldRelPath)))`; extract `projectName`, `systemClass` as strings (via the same `stringValue`-style guard); error `template %s@%s did not derive projectName/systemClass values` if absent. Set `model.Name = kebab`, `model.ProjectName`, `model.SystemClass`.
7. Placeholder existence check (Step 2 safety check) → `writeTopicsFile` → `writeSystemClassFile`.
8. `insertProjectReference(filepath.Join(opts.OutputDir, projectName+".SystemHost.csproj"), include)` — error if the csproj file is missing.
9. Summary to `Stderr`: `assembled system 'order-flow': 2 components, 1 topic, contracts from Models/` and `created <outputDir>` (the `template.Create` fetch/create lines already appeared).
10. `maybeWriteCreateResult` (same shape as deploy/create.go:188 — factor or copy the small stdout-vs-file writer).

---

## Step 5: command wiring — `cmd/intropy/sys.go` + `cmd/intropy/sys_create.go`

**`cmd/intropy/sys.go`** (mirror int.go/manifests.go):

```go
var sysCmd = &cobra.Command{
    Use:   "sys",
    Short: "Manage integration systems",
    Long:  "Manage Intropy integration systems — assemble scaffolded integrations into a system host.",
}
func init() { rootCmd.AddCommand(sysCmd) }
```

**`cmd/intropy/sys_create.go`**:

```go
type sysCreateFlags struct {
    name       string
    output     string
    version    string
    force      bool
    outputJSON string
}
var sysCreateFlagValues sysCreateFlags

var sysCreateCmd = &cobra.Command{
    Use:   "create",
    Short: "Assemble scaffolded integrations into a system host",
    Long:  "Scan the workspace for integration scaffold records (" + template.ScaffoldRelPath + "), render the system-host template, and assemble the typed system declaration (Topics.cs and the ISystemDefinition class) from what the scaffolds recorded. Run it from the workspace root that contains the scaffolded components and the shared Models project.",
    Args:  cobra.NoArgs,
    RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
        ctx, cancel := signal.NotifyContext(cmd.Context(), os.Interrupt, syscall.SIGTERM)
        defer cancel()
        return system.Create(ctx, system.CreateOptions{
            Name:       sysCreateFlagValues.name,
            OutputDir:  sysCreateFlagValues.output,
            Version:    sysCreateFlagValues.version,
            Force:      sysCreateFlagValues.force,
            OutputJSON: sysCreateFlagValues.outputJSON,
            Stdout:     cmd.OutOrStdout(),
            Stderr:     cmd.ErrOrStderr(),
            UserAgent:  "intropy-cli/" + version,
        })
    },
}

func init() {
    f := sysCreateCmd.Flags()
    f.StringVarP(&sysCreateFlagValues.name, "name", "n", "", "system name; PascalCase or kebab-case (OrderFlow and order-flow are equivalent)")
    f.StringVarP(&sysCreateFlagValues.output, "output", "o", "", "destination directory (defaults to the kebab-cased name)")
    f.StringVar(&sysCreateFlagValues.version, "version", "", "system-host template release tag (default: latest)")
    f.BoolVar(&sysCreateFlagValues.force, "force", false, "allow rendering into a non-empty output directory")
    f.StringVar(&sysCreateFlagValues.outputJSON, "output-json", "", "write a machine-readable result document to this path (- for stdout)")
    _ = sysCreateCmd.MarkFlagRequired("name")
    sysCmd.AddCommand(sysCreateCmd)
}
```

Deliberately **no** `-s/--set`, `-f/--values`, `--no-input` (template contract: only `name`, never prompts). Cobra's `required flag(s)` error already maps to exit 2 via `isCobraUsageError` (main.go:47). The kebab derivation lives in `system.Create` (so the internal package is the single source of the name semantics), not in the cmd layer.

**go.mod**: move `github.com/huandu/xstrings v1.5.0` from indirect to direct require (no version change).

---

## Step 6: docs

- **README.md** command tree (~line 165): add between `manifests` and `skills`:
  ```
  ├── sys                    Manage integration systems
  │   └── create                 Assemble scaffolded integrations into a system host
  ```
  Plus a short "Systems (`intropy sys`)" section following the existing per-noun sections: what it scans, the flag table, the tutorial example invocation.

---

## Test plan

**Step 0 tests** (internal/template): `TestCreateWritesBlockKind` — template YAML with the two labels; assert `Scaffold.BlockKind`/`DataFlow` round-trip. Same via a dependency in dependencies_test.go.

**`internal/system/assemble_test.go`** (pure, no network):
- Happy path: three entries (extractor, loader, shared-models built via `template.ScaffoldEntry` literals or `template.WriteScaffold` + `ListScaffolds` in a tempdir) → 2 components, 1 topic `{pubsub, orders, Order, Orders}`, shared `{Models}`.
- Shared topic dedup: extractor+loader on same `(pubsub, topic)` → one topic.
- Distinct pubsubs → two topics.
- Error table tests: zero components (`errors.Is(err, ErrNoComponents)`); missing `values.contract` (message contains record path and `values.contract`); numeric `topic` value (float64 → "has type float64, expected string"); duplicate appIds; conflicting contracts; zero shared libraries; two shared libraries; topic field collision.
- Warning tests: no blockKind → warnf called, entry skipped, assembly still succeeds; blockKind `reconciler` → skipped; role `system-host` → skipped.
- `pascalIdent` table: `orders`→`Orders`, `order-events`→`OrderEvents`.
- Kebab parity test: for inputs `{"OrderFlow", "order-flow", "OrderFlow2"}` assert `xstrings.ToKebabCase(in)` equals rendering `{{ . | kebabcase }}` through sprig (locks the parity assumption against future sprig upgrades).

**`internal/system/create_test.go`** (httptest stub, modeled on `newTemplateServer` / deploy's `newManifestsServer`; the package needs its own `buildTarGz` copy like deploy has):
- Stub serves a minimal but faithful system-host tarball: real `template.yaml` content (with the `projectName`/`systemClass`/`pubsub` derivations and the DNS-1123 pattern) + skeleton containing `Topics.cs.tmpl` placeholder, `{{ .systemClass }}.cs.tmpl` placeholder, `{{ .projectName }}.SystemHost.csproj.tmpl` (trimmed but with the Exists-guarded ItemGroup and `</Project>`), `Program.cs`.
- Workspace fixtures via `template.WriteScaffold`: `orders-extractor/` (BlockKind extractor, values appId/topic/contract/pubsub), `orders-loader/`, `Models/` (Role shared-library, values name=Models).
- Happy path (`Name: "OrderFlow"`, `OutputDir: system-host`): assert
  - `system-host/Topics.cs` equals the exact expected file (inline expected string — the repo has no golden-file convention, verified by grep, so inline literals it is),
  - `system-host/OrderFlowSystem.cs` equals expected (SystemName `order-flow`, both builder lines in order),
  - csproj contains the `../Models/Models.csproj` ProjectReference before `</Project>`,
  - `system-host/.intropy/scaffold.json` exists with `role: system-host`, values include `systemClass: OrderFlowSystem`,
  - `--output-json -` stdout parses and carries `system.components`/`system.topics`.
- Default output dir = `order-flow` when `-o` absent.
- Non-empty output dir without Force → error mentions `--force`; with Force + pre-existing host record in the walk → succeeds and stderr carries the skip warning.
- Missing-contract workspace → error before any HTTP request hits the stub (assert with a request-counting handler).
- Systemclass-mismatch defense: stub whose template.yaml derives `systemClass: 'Weird'` while skeleton file is named differently → the "template rendered no ... placeholder" error. (Simplest: skeleton with a literal `Other.cs` name.)

**`cmd/intropy/sys_create_test.go`**: run `rootCmd` in-process (`resetRootIO`, `t.Chdir`): `sys create` without `-n` → error, `exitCode(err) == 2`; `sys create -n X -s foo=bar` → `unknown flag` (locks the no-`--set` surface). Full end-to-end stays in the internal package (the GitHub seam isn't a flag, same split as manifests).

---

## Companion changes in `intropy-templates` (separate repo, must release before sys create is usable against latest)

1. **extractor/template.yaml + loader/template.yaml** — add to `spec.values`:
   ```yaml
   contract: 'Order'   # the shared-models contract type this component's topic carries
   pubsub: 'pubsub'    # the pub/sub component name; must stay in sync with Constants.cs PubSubName
   ```
   (extractor skeleton hardcodes `PubSubName = "pubsub"` in src/Configuration/Constants.cs.tmpl — recording it keeps the CLI free of the literal; the CLI still defaults to `"pubsub"` for records predating this change.)
2. **system-host/skeleton/`{{ .projectName }}`.SystemHost.csproj.tmpl** — delete the Exists-guarded `<ProjectName>.Contracts` ItemGroup: dead per the tutorial (host references `Models/`, inserted by the CLI; templates never hardcode project references).
3. **system-host/README.md + template.yaml description** — both still describe codegen generating "the sibling `<Project>.Contracts/` project" and `Apis.cs`/`Connectors.cs`; update to: v1 codegen owns `Topics.cs` + `<SystemClass>.cs` and inserts a reference to the workspace's shared-library project.
4. **system-host/skeleton/Topics.cs.tmpl placeholder comment** — references "the contract record in the Contracts project"; update to Models.

## Risks / inconsistencies found while reading

- **Namespace mismatch (needs an explicit call)**: the skeleton placeholders declare `namespace {{ .projectName }}.SystemHost;` but the tutorial's assembled `Topics.cs`/`OrderFlowSystem.cs` have **no namespace**. Plan follows the tutorial (spec): codegen emits namespace-less files; both generated files are internally consistent and discovery reflects over the assembly regardless. A direct render followed by `sys create` therefore changes the files' namespace — harmless, but the skeleton placeholders should ideally drop their namespace too (add to companion change 4) so the two states diff minimally.
- **`title` derivation fragility**: system-host derives `projectName` via deprecated `strings.Title` (sprig v3.3.0). Reading back the host scaffold record sidesteps it entirely; the mismatch defense in Step 2 catches any future template/CLI divergence at create time instead of at .NET discovery time.
- **Old scaffold records**: workspaces scaffolded before Step 0 ships have no `blockKind` → everything is skipped and `sys create` reports "no assemblable integration scaffolds". The skip warning's "re-scaffold with a newer template release" text is the mitigation; worth a line in the tutorial's info admonition.
- **`contract` value staleness**: with `empty: true` scaffolds, shared-models still emits an `Order` record shell, so `contract: 'Order'` stays valid — but if a user renames the contract type in Models/ later, `sys create` re-runs generate a stale `TopicRef<Order>`. Acceptable v1: the host's `check` gate catches it at compile time.
- **Tutorial listing detail**: tutorial `Topics.cs` shows a hand-written per-topic doc comment; codegen emits a generic deterministic one (see Step 2). Either accept the diff or align the tutorial listing when this lands.

### Critical Files for Implementation
- /Users/robinhultman/dev/intropy/tooling/intropy-cli/internal/template/scaffold.go (Step 0 fields/labels; `WriteScaffold`/`LoadScaffold` reused throughout)
- /Users/robinhultman/dev/intropy/tooling/intropy-cli/internal/template/create.go (the `Create`/`CreateOptions` machinery sys create wraps; writer call site at line 116)
- /Users/robinhultman/dev/intropy/tooling/intropy-cli/internal/deploy/create.go (structural precedent for the new internal/system package: options seams, result JSON, error style)

13		// understands. Bump only for incompatible changes; additive fields do
14		// not require a bump.
15		ScaffoldSchemaVersion = 1
16	
17		// ScaffoldRelPath is where the scaffold record lives inside a project.
18		ScaffoldRelPath = ".intropy/scaffold.json"
19	
20		// TemplateRoleLabel names the manifest label that declares what role a
21		// template's output plays in a system. Its value is copied into the
22		// scaffold record so later commands can tell support projects apart
23		// from system blocks.

27		// referenced by sibling components (e.g. shared models). System
28		// assembly must not treat it as a block.
29		RoleSharedLibrary = "shared-library"
30	)

32	var ErrScaffoldNotFound = errors.New("no " + ScaffoldRelPath + " found in current directory or any parent")
33	
34	// Scaffold is the committed record of what `int create` rendered. Unlike
35	// CreateResult it carries no outputDir — the file's location is the project
36	// root — and it is written into the project so later commands (e.g.
37	// `manifests create`) can re-fetch the exact template version.
38	type Scaffold struct {
39		SchemaVersion int            `json:"schemaVersion"`
40		Template      string         `json:"template"` // directory name in the template library repo
41		Owner         string         `json:"owner"`
42		Repo          string         `json:"repo"`
43		Version       string         `json:"version"`
44		Values        map[string]any `json:"values"`
45

47		// if any (e.g. "shared-library").
48		Role string `json:"role,omitempty"`
49	
50		// DependsOn lists the sibling projects this project's template declared
51		// under spec.dependencies, whether the render created them or they
52		// already existed.
53		DependsOn []DependencyRecord `json:"dependsOn,omitempty"`
54	}
55	
56	// DependencyRecord points at a sibling project a component depends on. Dir
57	// is slash-separated and relative to the component root (e.g. "../Acme.Models").
58	type DependencyRecord struct {
59		Template string `json:"template"`
60		Dir      string `json:"dir"`
61	}

63	func roleFromLabels(labels map[string]string) string {
64		return labels[TemplateRoleLabel]
65	}

67	// WriteScaffold writes the scaffold record to <projectRoot>/.intropy/scaffold.json.
68	func WriteScaffold(projectRoot string, s Scaffold) error {
69		path := filepath.Join(projectRoot, filepath.FromSlash(ScaffoldRelPath))
70		if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(path), 0o755); err != nil {
71			return fmt.Errorf("write scaffold record: %w", err)
72		}
73		data, err := json.MarshalIndent(s, "", "  ")
74		if err != nil {
75			return fmt.Errorf("write scaffold record: %w", err)
76		}
77		data = append(data, '\n')
78		if err := os.WriteFile(path, data, 0o644); err != nil {
79			return fmt.Errorf("write scaffold record: %w", err)
80		}
81		return nil
82	}
83	
84	// LoadScaffold reads and parses a scaffold.json file.
85	func LoadScaffold(path string) (*Scaffold, error) {
86		data, err := os.ReadFile(path)
87		if err != nil {
88			return nil, fmt.Errorf("read scaffold record %s: %w", path, err)
89		}
90		var s Scaffold
91		if err := json.Unmarshal(data, &s); err != nil {
92			return nil, fmt.Errorf("parse scaffold record %s: %w", path, err)
93		}
94		return &s, nil
95	}
96	
97	// FindScaffold walks up from startDir looking for .intropy/scaffold.json.
98	// Returns the parsed record and the project root that contains it, or
99	// ErrScaffoldNotFound if the filesystem root is reached first.
100	func FindScaffold(startDir string) (*Scaffold, string, error) {
101		abs, err := filepath.Abs(startDir)
102		if err != nil {
103			return nil, "", fmt.Errorf("absolute path: %w", err)
104		}
105	
106		for {
107			candidate := filepath.Join(abs, filepath.FromSlash(ScaffoldRelPath))
108			if _, err := os.Stat(candidate); err == nil {
109				s, err := LoadScaffold(candidate)
110				if err != nil {
111					return nil, "", err
112				}
113				return s, abs, nil
114			} else if !os.IsNotExist(err) {
115				return nil, "", fmt.Errorf("stat %s: %w", candidate, err)
116			}
117	
118			parent := filepath.Dir(abs)
119			if parent == abs {
120				return nil, "", ErrScaffoldNotFound
121			}
122			abs = parent
123		}
124	}

# Implement `intropy sys create`

## Context

Chapter 3 of the "Compose a system" tutorial (`intropy-techdocs/docs/tutorials/system/03-systemhost.md`, served at http://127.0.0.1:8000/tutorials/system/) specifies a new command: `intropy sys create -n OrderFlow -o system-host`. Run from a workspace root, it scans for the `.intropy/scaffold.json` records that `int create` left behind (extractor/loader blocks + the shared `Models/` library), renders the existing `system-host` template (Aspire AppHost shell with compilable placeholders), and **assembles the typed system declaration**: `Topics.cs` (one `TopicRef<T>` per topic) and `<Name>System.cs` (`ISystemDefinition` wiring components via `SystemBuilder`). Edges are derived from components sharing a topic. The host references the workspace's `Models/` project for contract types — it never generates its own contract.

Everything downstream exists and is tested: the `system-host` template (`intropy-templates/system-host/`, renders with only a kebab `name`, derives `projectName`/`systemClass`/`pubsub` via sprig) and the .NET side (`SystemBuilder`, `TopicRef<T>`, `IntropyAspire.RunAsync`, `IntropyGenerate.RunAsync` in `tooling/Intropy.Topology`).

**Decisions confirmed with user:**
- Contract type per topic comes from a `contract` value recorded in scaffold.json (companion change in intropy-templates); no heuristics, no C# parsing.
- Records lacking `blockKind` are skipped with a warning telling the user to re-scaffold (no template-name fallback).
- v1 scope: extractor + loader only; other block kinds skipped with warning. No `Apis.cs`/`Connectors.cs`.
- Host references the existing shared-library project (`Models/`); the CLI inserts the `ProjectReference` (templates never hardcode cross-project refs).

## Step 0 — prerequisite: record block-kind/data-flow labels (own commit)

The templates already declare `intropy.dev/block-kind: extractor|loader` and `intropy.dev/data-flow` labels; the CLI only copies `template-role`. Docs claim otherwise — confirmed gap.

- `internal/template/scaffold.go`: add constants `TemplateBlockKindLabel`, `TemplateDataFlowLabel`, `BlockKindExtractor`, `BlockKindLoader`; add `BlockKind`/`DataFlow` string fields to `Scaffold` (json `blockKind,omitempty` / `dataFlow,omitempty` — additive, no schemaVersion bump per comment at scaffold.go:12); helpers next to `roleFromLabels` (scaffold.go:63).
- Populate at both writer sites: `internal/template/create.go:116` and `internal/template/dependencies.go:132`.
- Tests: extend scaffold-writing tests in `internal/template/create_test.go` + `dependencies_test.go` with labeled template fixtures.

## Step 1 — `internal/system` package: assemble (pure logic)

New package modeled on `internal/deploy` (thin consumer of `internal/template`).

`internal/system/model.go`: `TopicKey{Pubsub, Name}`, `Topic{TopicKey, Contract, Field}`, `Component{AppID, Kind, Topic TopicKey, Path}`, `SharedLibrary{Path, Name}`, `Model{Name, ProjectName, SystemClass, Components, Topics, Shared}`.

`internal/system/assemble.go`:
```go
func Assemble(entries []template.ScaffoldEntry, warnf func(string, ...any)) (*Model, error)
```
- Classify: role `shared-library` → contract project; role `system-host` → skip w/ warning (keeps `--force` re-runs sane); blockKind extractor/loader → component; other blockKind → skip w/ warning ("sys create assembles extractors and loaders only"); neither → skip w/ warning ("no block kind — re-scaffold with a newer release").
- Extract values via a `stringValue(entry, key)` helper with errors naming the record path and actual type (JSON round-trip makes numbers `float64`). Required: `appId`, `topic`, `contract` (missing `contract` → guidance to re-scaffold or add `"contract": "<TypeName>"` by hand). Optional `pubsub`, default `"pubsub"`.
- Validate: zero components → sentinel `ErrNoComponents` with guidance; duplicate `appId`s → error naming both dirs; same `(pubsub, topic)` with conflicting contracts → error; zero shared libraries → error (tutorial guarantees Models/ via template dependencies); >1 shared library → error (ambiguous `using` + ProjectReference); topic field-name collision after PascalCase → error.
- Topics sorted by `(Pubsub, Name)`; `Field = pascalIdent(topic)` (`"orders"`→`"Orders"`, `"order-events"`→`"OrderEvents"`).

## Step 2 — codegen: `internal/system/codegen.go`

Embedded `text/template` const strings (no sprig). Output matches tutorial: **namespace-less** files (placeholders carry `namespace {{ .projectName }}.SystemHost;`, tutorial output has none — follow the tutorial; see companion change 4).

- `writeTopicsFile(dir, m)` — overwrites `Topics.cs`: `using Intropy.Topology;` + `using <Shared.Name>;`, `public static class Topics` with one `public static readonly TopicRef<Order> Orders = TopicRef<Order>.Define("pubsub", "orders");` per topic, generic doc comment per topic.
- `writeSystemClassFile(dir, m)` — overwrites `<SystemClass>.cs`: `public sealed class OrderFlowSystem : ISystemDefinition`, `SystemName => "order-flow"`, `Define(SystemBuilder builder)` with `builder.AddExtractor("<appId>").Publishes(Topics.<Field>);` / `AddLoader(...).Subscribes(...)`.
- **Safety gate**: before writing, stat `<dir>/<SystemClass>.cs`; if the template didn't render that placeholder, fail ("template's systemClass derivation disagrees with this CLI") — prevents the two-`ISystemDefinition` discovery failure the template.yaml:30-32 comment warns about.

## Step 3 — csproj reference insertion: `internal/system/csproj.go`

`insertProjectReference(csprojPath, include string) error` — string insertion of an `ItemGroup` with `<ProjectReference Include="../Models/Models.csproj" IsAspireProjectResource="false" />` before the last `</Project>` (verified: rendered csproj is hand-formatted XML with comments; `encoding/xml` would destroy it; `IsAspireProjectResource="false"` required or Aspire treats it as a resource). Include path from `filepath.Rel(outputDir, shared.Path)` + `shared.Name + ".csproj"`, slash-separated.

## Step 4 — orchestration: `internal/system/create.go`

`CreateOptions{Name, StartDir, OutputDir, Version, Force, OutputJSON, Stdout, Stderr, HTTP, UserAgent, Owner/Repo/GitHubBaseURL}` (same test seams as `internal/deploy/create.go`). `CreateResult` mirrors `template.CreateResult` + `System` summary (components/topics/sharedLibrary — loosely mirrors `dotnet run -- graph`).

`Create(ctx, opts)` sequence (all local validation before network I/O):
1. `kebab := xstrings.ToKebabCase(opts.Name)` — exact parity with sprig's `kebabcase` (sprig v3.3.0 delegates to xstrings; `github.com/huandu/xstrings v1.5.0` already in go.mod as indirect → promote to direct). Default `OutputDir` to kebab. The template's DNS-1123 `pattern` on `name` handles remaining format validation during Resolve.
2. `template.ListScaffolds(opts.StartDir)` → warnings to Stderr → `Assemble`.
3. Compute csproj include path (fail early).

# Implement `intropy sys create`

## Context

Chapter 3 of the "Compose a system" tutorial (`intropy-techdocs/docs/tutorials/system/03-systemhost.md`, served at http://127.0.0.1:8000/tutorials/system/) specifies a new command: `intropy sys create -n OrderFlow -o system-host`. Run from a workspace root, it scans for the `.intropy/scaffold.json` records that `int create` left behind (extractor/loader blocks + the shared `Models/` library), renders the existing `system-host` template (Aspire AppHost shell with compilable placeholders), and **assembles the typed system declaration**: `Topics.cs` (one `TopicRef<T>` per topic) and `<Name>System.cs` (`ISystemDefinition` wiring components via `SystemBuilder`). Edges are derived from components sharing a topic. The host references the workspace's `Models/` project for contract types — it never generates its own contract.

Everything downstream exists and is tested: the `system-host` template (`intropy-templates/system-host/`, renders with only a kebab `name`, derives `projectName`/`systemClass`/`pubsub` via sprig) and the .NET side (`SystemBuilder`, `TopicRef<T>`, `IntropyAspire.RunAsync`, `IntropyGenerate.RunAsync` in `tooling/Intropy.Topology`).

**Decisions confirmed with user:**
- Contract type per topic comes from a `contract` value recorded in scaffold.json (companion change in intropy-templates); no heuristics, no C# parsing.
- Records lacking `blockKind` are skipped with a warning telling the user to re-scaffold (no template-name fallback).
- v1 scope: extractor + loader only; other block kinds skipped with warning. No `Apis.cs`/`Connectors.cs`.
- Host references the existing shared-library project (`Models/`); the CLI inserts the `ProjectReference` (templates never hardcode cross-project refs).

## Step 0 — prerequisite: record block-kind/data-flow labels (own commit)

The templates already declare `intropy.dev/block-kind: extractor|loader` and `intropy.dev/data-flow` labels; the CLI only copies `template-role`. Docs claim otherwise — confirmed gap.

- `internal/template/scaffold.go`: add constants `TemplateBlockKindLabel`, `TemplateDataFlowLabel`, `BlockKindExtractor`, `BlockKindLoader`; add `BlockKind`/`DataFlow` string fields to `Scaffold` (json `blockKind,omitempty` / `dataFlow,omitempty` — additive, no schemaVersion bump per comment at scaffold.go:12); helpers next to `roleFromLabels` (scaffold.go:63).
- Populate at both writer sites: `internal/template/create.go:116` and `internal/template/dependencies.go:132`.
- Tests: extend scaffold-writing tests in `internal/template/create_test.go` + `dependencies_test.go` with labeled template fixtures.

## Step 1 — `internal/system` package: assemble (pure logic)

New package modeled on `internal/deploy` (thin consumer of `internal/template`).

`internal/system/model.go`: `TopicKey{Pubsub, Name}`, `Topic{TopicKey, Contract, Field}`, `Component{AppID, Kind, Topic TopicKey, Path}`, `SharedLibrary{Path, Name}`, `Model{Name, ProjectName, SystemClass, Components, Topics, Shared}`.

`internal/system/assemble.go`:
```go
func Assemble(entries []template.ScaffoldEntry, warnf func(string, ...any)) (*Model, error)
```
- Classify: role `shared-library` → contract project; role `system-host` → skip w/ warning (keeps `--force` re-runs sane); blockKind extractor/loader → component; other blockKind → skip w/ warning ("sys create assembles extractors and loaders only"); neither → skip w/ warning ("no block kind — re-scaffold with a newer release").
- Extract values via a `stringValue(entry, key)` helper with errors naming the record path and actual type (JSON round-trip makes numbers `float64`). Required: `appId`, `topic`, `contract` (missing `contract` → guidance to re-scaffold or add `"contract": "<TypeName>"` by hand). Optional `pubsub`, default `"pubsub"`.

Embedded `text/template` const strings (no sprig). Output matches tutorial: **namespace-less** files (placeholders carry `namespace {{ .projectName }}.SystemHost;`, tutorial output has none — follow the tutorial; see companion change 4).

## Step 3 — csproj reference insertion: `internal/system/csproj.go`

`insertProjectReference(csprojPath, include string) error` — string insertion of an `ItemGroup` with `<ProjectReference Include="../Models/Models.csproj" IsAspireProjectResource="false" />` before the last `</Project>` (verified: rendered csproj is hand-formatted XML with comments; `encoding/xml` would destroy it; `IsAspireProjectResource="false"` required or Aspire treats it as a resource). Base directory for this skill: /Users/robinhultman/.claude/skills/golang-cli

**Persona:** You are a Go CLI engineer. You build tools that feel native to the Unix shell — composable, scriptable, and predictable under automation.

**Modes:**

- **Build** — creating a new CLI from scratch: follow the project structure, root command setup, flag binding, and version embedding sections sequentially.
- **Extend** — adding subcommands, flags, or completions to an existing CLI: read the current command tree first, then apply changes consistent with the existing structure.
- **Review** — auditing an existing CLI for correctness: check the Common Mistakes table, verify `SilenceUsage`/`SilenceErrors`, flag-to-Viper binding, exit codes, and stdout/stderr discipline.

# Go CLI Best Practices

Use Cobra + Viper as the default stack for Go CLI applications. Cobra provides the command/subcommand/flag structure and Viper handles configuration from files, environment variables, and flags with automatic layering. This combination powers kubectl, docker, gh, hugo, and most production Go CLIs.

When using Cobra or Viper, refer to the library's official documentation and code examples for current API signatures.

For trivial single-purpose tools with no subcommands and few flags, stdlib `flag` is sufficient.

## Quick Reference

| Concern             | Package / Tool                       |
| ------------------- | ------------------------------------ |
| Commands & flags    | `github.com/spf13/cobra`             |
| Configuration       | `github.com/spf13/viper`             |
| Flag parsing        | `github.com/spf13/pflag` (via Cobra) |
| Colored output      | `github.com/fatih/color`             |
| Table output        | `github.com/olekukonko/tablewriter`  |
| Interactive prompts | `github.com/charmbracelet/bubbletea` |
| Version injection   | `go build -ldflags`                  |
| Distribution        | `goreleaser`                         |

## Project Structure

Organize CLI commands in `cmd/myapp/` with one file per command. Keep `main.go` minimal — it only calls `Execute()`.

```
myapp/
├── cmd/
│   └── myapp/
│       ├── main.go              # package main, only calls Execute()
│       ├── root.go              # Root command + Viper init
│       ├── serve.go             # "serve" subcommand
│       ├── migrate.go           # "migrate" subcommand
│       └── version.go           # "version" subcommand
├── go.mod
└── go.sum
```

`main.go` should be minimal — see [assets/examples/main.go](assets/examples/main.go).

## Root Command Setup

The root command initializes Viper configuration and sets up global behavior via `PersistentPreRunE`. See [assets/examples/root.go](assets/examples/root.go).

Key points:

- `SilenceUsage: true` MUST be set — prevents printing the full usage text on every error
- `SilenceErrors: true` MUST be set — lets you control error output format yourself
- `PersistentPreRunE` runs before every subcommand, so config is always initialized
- Logs go to stderr, output goes to stdout

## Subcommands

Add subcommands by creating separate files in `cmd/myapp/` and registering them in `init()`. See [assets/examples/serve.go](assets/examples/serve.go) for a complete subcommand example including command groups.

## Flags

See [assets/examples/flags.go](assets/examples/flags.go) for all flag patterns:

### Persistent vs Local

- **Persistent** flags are inherited by all subcommands (e.g., `--config`)
- **Local** flags only apply to the command they're defined on (e.g., `--port`)

### Required Flags

Use `MarkFlagRequired`, `MarkFlagsMutuallyExclusive`, and `MarkFlagsOneRequired` for flag constraints.

### Flag Validation with RegisterFlagCompletionFunc

Provide completion suggestions for flag values.

### Always Bind Flags to Viper

This ensures `viper.GetInt("port")` returns the flag value, env var `MYAPP_PORT`, or config file value — whichever has highest precedence.

## Argument Validation

Cobra provides built-in validators for positional arguments. See [assets/examples/args.go](assets/examples/args.go) for both built-in and custom validation examples.

| Validator                   | Description                          |
| --------------------------- | ------------------------------------ |
| `cobra.NoArgs`              | Fails if any args provided           |
| `cobra.ExactArgs(n)`        | Requires exactly n args              |
| `cobra.MinimumNArgs(n)`     | Requires at least n args             |
| `cobra.MaximumNArgs(n)`     | Allows at most n args                |
| `cobra.RangeArgs(min, max)` | Requires between min and max         |
| `cobra.ExactValidArgs(n)`   | Exactly n args, must be in ValidArgs |

## Configuration with Viper

Viper resolves configuration values in this order (highest to lowest precedence):

1. **CLI flags** (explicit user input)
2. **Environment variables** (deployment config)
3. **Config file** (persistent settings)
4. **Defaults** (set in code)

See [assets/examples/config.go](assets/examples/config.go) for complete Viper integration including struct unmarshaling and config file watching.

### Example Config File (.myapp.yaml)

```yaml
port: 8080
host: localhost
log-level: info
database:
  dsn: postgres://localhost:5432/myapp
  max-conn: 25
```

With the setup above, these are all equivalent:

- Flag: `--port 9090`
- Env var: `MYAPP_PORT=9090`
- Config file: `port: 9090`

## Version and Build Info

Version SHOULD be embedded at compile time using `ldflags`. See [assets/examples/version.go](assets/examples/version.go) for the version command and build instructions.

## Exit Codes

Exit codes MUST follow Unix conventions:

| Code  | Meaning           | When to Use                               |
| ----- | ----------------- | ----------------------------------------- |
| 0     | Success           | Operation completed normally              |
| 1     | General error     | Runtime failure                           |
| 2     | Usage error       | Invalid flags or arguments                |
| 64-78 | BSD sysexits      | Specific error categories                 |
| 126   | Cannot execute    | Permission denied                         |
| 127   | Command not found | Missing dependency                        |
| 128+N | Signal N          | Terminated by signal (e.g., 130 = SIGINT) |

See [assets/examples/exit_codes.go](assets/examples/exit_codes.go) for a pattern mapping errors to exit codes.

## I/O Patterns

See [assets/examples/output.go](assets/examples/output.go) for all I/O patterns:

- **stdout vs stderr**: NEVER write diagnostic output to stdout — stdout is for program output (pipeable), stderr for logs/errors/diagnostics
- **Detecting pipe vs terminal**: check `os.ModeCharDevice` on stdout
- **Machine-readable output**: support `--output` flag for table/json/plain formats
- **Colors**: use `fatih/color` which auto-disables when output is not a terminal

## Signal Handling

Signal handling MUST use `signal.NotifyContext` to propagate cancellation through context. See [assets/examples/signal.go](assets/examples/signal.go) for graceful HTTP server shutdown.

## Shell Completions

Cobra generates completions for bash, zsh, fish, and PowerShell automatically. See [assets/examples/completion.go](assets/examples/completion.go) for both the completion command and custom flag/argument completions.

## Testing CLI Commands

Test commands by executing them programmatically and capturing output. See [assets/examples/cli_test.go](assets/examples/cli_test.go).

Use `cmd.OutOrStdout()` and `cmd.ErrOrStderr()` in commands (instead of `os.Stdout` / `os.Stderr`) so output can be captured in tests.

## Common Mistakes

| Mistake | Fix |
| --- | --- |
| Writing to `os.Stdout` directly | Tests can't capture output. Use `cmd.OutOrStdout()` which tests can redirect to a buffer |
| Calling `os.Exit()` inside `RunE` | Cobra's error handling, deferred functions, and cleanup code never run. Return an error, let `main()` decide |
| Not binding flags to Viper | Flags won't be configurable via env/config. Call `viper.BindPFlag` for every configurable flag |
| Missing `viper.SetEnvPrefix` | `PORT` collides with other tools. Use a prefix (`MYAPP_PORT`) to namespace env vars |
| Logging to stdout | Unix pipes chain stdout — logs corrupt the data stream for the next program. Logs go to stderr |
| Printing usage on every error | Full help text on every error is noise. Set `SilenceUsage: true`, save full usage for `--help` |
| Config file required | Users without a config file get a crash. Ignore `viper.ConfigFileNotFoundError` — config should be optional |
| Not using `PersistentPreRunE` | Config initialization must happen before any subcommand. Use root's `PersistentPreRunE` |
| Hardcoded version string | Version gets out of sync with tags. Inject via `ldflags` at build time from git tags |
| Not supporting `--output` format | Scripts can't parse human-readable output. Add JSON/table/plain for machine consumption |

## Related Skills

See `samber/cc-skills-golang@golang-project-layout`, `samber/cc-skills-golang@golang-dependency-injection`, `samber/cc-skills-golang@golang-testing`, `samber/cc-skills-golang@golang-design-patterns` skills.

package template

import (
	"bytes"
	"context"
	"encoding/json"
	"net/http"
	"net/http/httptest"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"strings"
	"testing"
)

const depComponentYAML = `apiVersion: intropy.dev/v1
kind: Template
metadata:
  name: component
spec:
  parameters:
    type: object
    required: [name]
    properties:
      name:
        type: string
      org:
        type: string
        default: Acme
  dependencies:
    - template: shared
      output: '{{ .org }}.Models'
      values:
        name: '{{ .org }}.Models'
`

const depSharedYAML = `apiVersion: intropy.dev/v1
kind: Template
metadata:
  name: shared
  labels:
    intropy.dev/template-role: shared-library
spec:
  parameters:
    type: object
    required: [name]
    properties:
      name:
        type: string
`

// newDependencyServer serves a tarball holding a component template that
// declares a dependency on the shared template in the same repo.
func newDependencyServer(t *testing.T, tag string, extra map[string]string) *httptest.Server {
	t.Helper()
	files := map[string]string{
		"component/template.yaml":           depComponentYAML,
		"component/skeleton/README.md.tmpl": "component {{ .name }}\n",
		"shared/template.yaml":              depSharedYAML,
		"shared/skeleton/lib.txt.tmpl":      "shared {{ .name }}\n",
	}
	for k, v := range extra {
		files[k] = v
	}
	tarball := buildTarGz(t, "owner-repo-abc123", files)
	mux := http.NewServeMux()
	mux.HandleFunc("/repos/o/r/tarball/"+tag, func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
		_, _ = w.Write(tarball)
	})
	return httptest.NewServer(mux)
}

func createComponent(t *testing.T, srv *httptest.Server, outDir string, stderr *bytes.Buffer, jsonPath string, force bool) error {
	t.Helper()
	return Create(context.Background(), CreateOptions{
		Template:      "component",
		OutputDir:     outDir,
		Version:       "v1",
		SetValues:     map[string]any{"name": "orders"},
		Force:         force,
		NoInput:       true,
		OutputJSON:    jsonPath,
		Stdout:        &bytes.Buffer{},
		Stderr:        stderr,
		HTTP:          srv.Client(),
		Owner:         "o",
		Repo:          "r",
		GitHubBaseURL: srv.URL,
	})
}

func TestCreateRendersMissingDependency(t *testing.T) {
	srv := newDependencyServer(t, "v1", nil)
	defer srv.Close()

	parent := t.TempDir()
	outDir := filepath.Join(parent, "orders")
	jsonPath := filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "result.json")
	var stderr bytes.Buffer

	if err := createComponent(t, srv, outDir, &stderr, jsonPath, false); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Create: %v\nstderr: %s", err, stderr.String())
	}

	lib, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(parent, "Acme.Models", "lib.txt"))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("dependency not rendered: %v", err)
	}
	if string(lib) != "shared Acme.Models\n" {
		t.Errorf("lib.txt = %q", string(lib))
	}

	depScaffold, err := LoadScaffold(filepath.Join(parent, "Acme.Models", filepath.FromSlash(ScaffoldRelPath)))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("dependency scaffold: %v", err)
	}
	if depScaffold.Template != "shared" || depScaffold.Role != RoleSharedLibrary || depScaffold.Version != "v1" {
		t.Errorf("dependency scaffold = %+v", depScaffold)
	}

	compScaffold, err := LoadScaffold(filepath.Join(outDir, filepath.FromSlash(ScaffoldRelPath)))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("component scaffold: %v", err)
	}
	want := DependencyRecord{Template: "shared", Dir: "../Acme.Models"}
	if len(compScaffold.DependsOn) != 1 || compScaffold.DependsOn[0] != want {
		t.Errorf("DependsOn = %+v", compScaffold.DependsOn)
	}

	var result CreateResult
	data, _ := os.ReadFile(jsonPath)

64	func buildTarGz(t *testing.T, prefix string, entries map[string]string) []byte {
65		t.Helper()
66		var buf bytes.Buffer
67		gz := gzip.NewWriter(&buf)
68		tw := tar.NewWriter(gz)
69		for name, content := range entries {
70			full := name
71			if prefix != "" {
72				full = prefix + "/" + name
73			}
74			h := &tar.Header{Name: full, Mode: 0o644, Size: int64(len(content)), Typeflag: tar.TypeReg}
75			if err := tw.WriteHeader(h); err != nil {
76				t.Fatal(err)
77			}
78			if _, err := tw.Write([]byte(content)); err != nil {
79				t.Fatal(err)
80			}
81		}
82		if err := tw.Close(); err != nil {
83			t.Fatal(err)
84		}
85		if err := gz.Close(); err != nil {
86			t.Fatal(err)
87		}
88		return buf.Bytes()
89	}

type manifestsCreateFlags struct {
	output     string
	version    string
	values     []string
	sets       []string
	force      bool
	noInput    bool
	outputJSON string
}

var manifestsCreateFlagValues manifestsCreateFlags

var manifestsCreateCmd = &cobra.Command{
	Use:   "create",
	Short: "Create Kubernetes manifests for a scaffolded integration",
	Long: "Generate a kustomize base + overlays tree of Kubernetes deployment manifests for a previously scaffolded integration. " +
		"Run it inside the integration project: the command walks up from the current directory to find " + template.ScaffoldRelPath + ", " +
		"re-fetches the exact template version recorded there, and renders its manifests/ templates. " +
		"Scaffold values (e.g. name, appPort) pre-fill matching manifest parameters; remaining required parameters are prompted for, or supplied via --set/--values.",
	Args: cobra.NoArgs,
	RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
		sets, err := template.ParseSets(manifestsCreateFlagValues.sets)
		if err != nil {
			return err
		}
		ctx, cancel := signal.NotifyContext(cmd.Context(), os.Interrupt, syscall.SIGTERM)
		defer cancel()
		return deploy.Create(ctx, deploy.CreateOptions{
			OutputDir:  manifestsCreateFlagValues.output,
			Version:    manifestsCreateFlagValues.version,
			SetValues:  sets,
			Files:      manifestsCreateFlagValues.values,
			Force:      manifestsCreateFlagValues.force,
			NoInput:    manifestsCreateFlagValues.noInput,
			OutputJSON: manifestsCreateFlagValues.outputJSON,
			Stdin:      cmd.InOrStdin(),
			Stdout:     cmd.OutOrStdout(),
			Stderr:     cmd.ErrOrStderr(),
			UserAgent:  "intropy-cli/" + version,
		})
	},
}

func init() {
	f := manifestsCreateCmd.Flags()
	f.StringVarP(&manifestsCreateFlagValues.output, "output", "o", "", "destination directory (default: deploy, relative to the project root)")
	f.StringVar(&manifestsCreateFlagValues.version, "version", "", "template release tag (default: the version pinned in "+template.ScaffoldRelPath+")")
	f.StringArrayVarP(&manifestsCreateFlagValues.values, "values", "f", nil, "values file in YAML/JSON (repeatable; use - to read one doc from stdin)")
	f.StringArrayVarP(&manifestsCreateFlagValues.sets, "set", "s", nil, "set a value as key=value (repeatable)")
	f.BoolVar(&manifestsCreateFlagValues.force, "force", false, "allow rendering into a non-empty output directory")
	f.BoolVar(&manifestsCreateFlagValues.noInput, "no-input", false, "disable interactive prompts for missing values")
	f.StringVar(&manifestsCreateFlagValues.outputJSON, "output-json", "", "write a machine-readable result document to this path (- for stdout)")
	manifestsCmd.AddCommand(manifestsCreateCmd)
}

## Deployment manifests (`intropy manifests`)

### Generate Kubernetes manifests

Run inside a scaffolded integration (any subdirectory works — the command
walks up to find `.intropy/scaffold.json`):

```sh
intropy manifests create
```

This re-fetches the template at the exact version pinned in
`.intropy/scaffold.json` and renders its `manifests/` templates into a
kustomize tree:

```
deploy/
├── base/                  Deployment + Service with Dapr sidecar annotations
│   ├── deployment.yaml
│   ├── service.yaml
│   └── kustomization.yaml
└── overlays/
    ├── dev/               Dapr components for local-style backends
    └── prod/              Real-broker placeholders, secrets via secretKeyRef
```

Values recorded at scaffold time (like `name` and `appPort`) pre-fill the
matching manifest parameters, so you're only asked for what's new — typically
the container image:

```sh
# inline
intropy manifests create --set imageRepository=ghcr.io/acme/orders --set imageTag=1.0.0

# non-interactive (fail fast on missing required values)
intropy manifests create --no-input -f deploy-values.yaml

# elsewhere than deploy/, or on top of existing files
intropy manifests create -o ./k8s --force

# newer template release than the one pinned at scaffold time
intropy manifests create --version v1.5.0

# machine-readable result document (consumed by chained tooling)
intropy manifests create --output-json -
```

Projects scaffolded before `.intropy/scaffold.json` existed get an error
explaining how to add the file by hand; templates whose pinned release
predates `manifests/` templates are told to pass `--version` with a newer
tag.

Validate the result with `kustomize build deploy/overlays/dev` (or point your
GitOps tooling at an overlay directly).
