## Systems (`intropy sys`)

### Assemble a system host

Run from the workspace root that holds your scaffolded integrations:

```sh
intropy sys create -n OrderFlow -o system-host
```

The command reads before it writes: it scans the workspace for the
`.intropy/scaffold.json` records the integration scaffolds left behind,
renders the `system-host` template (a .NET Aspire AppHost), and assembles
the typed system declaration from what the scaffolds recorded —
`Topics.cs` defines each topic once as a `TopicRef<T>`, and the
`ISystemDefinition` class wires every extractor and loader to its topic.
The workspace's shared contracts project (template role `shared-library`,
typically `Models/`) is referenced from the host, never declared as a
component.

`-n` accepts PascalCase or kebab-case — `OrderFlow` kebab-cases to
`order-flow`, the system's name. Unlike `int create` there are no `--set`
or values flags: the template renders with only the name, and everything
else comes from the scaffold records.

```sh
# default output directory: the kebab-cased name (./order-flow)
intropy sys create -n OrderFlow

# pin the system-host template release
intropy sys create -n OrderFlow -o system-host --version v1.5.0

# machine-readable result document with the assembled model
intropy sys create -n OrderFlow -o system-host --output-json -
```

Records without a `blockKind` (scaffolded by an older CLI) or with a block
kind other than extractor/loader are skipped with a warning. Validate the
result from the host directory with `dotnet run -- check`.

  description: Long-running .NET extractor that polls a local source folder, runs each file through the Intropy extractor pipeline, and publishes the result as a CloudEvent to a Dapr pub/sub topic.
  tags:

spec:

    type: object
    required:
      - name
      - organization
      - topic
    properties:
      name:
        type: string
        title: Project name
        description: PascalCase identifier used for the .NET project, root namespace, and assembly. Dot-separated segments are allowed for nested namespaces (e.g. OrderExtractor or Int1055.OrderExtractor).
        pattern: "^[A-Z][A-Za-z0-9]*(\\.[A-Z][A-Za-z0-9]*)*$"

        type: string
        title: Organization
        description: PascalCase name of the organization the integration runs for. Becomes the telemetry ServiceNamespace and the business-incident source URN (urn:<organization>:<component>).

        type: string

        description: The pub/sub topic the extractor publishes to. This is the extractor's half of the system contract — scaffold the consuming loader with the same value.

content.content:
1	# system-host
2	
3	The Aspire host project of an Intropy integration system: a .NET Aspire
4	AppHost whose one job is to hold the system's source of truth — a typed C#
5	declaration of which components exist and which topics connect them — and to
6	run, validate, or generate the system from that one declaration.
7	
8	This template is normally rendered by **`intropy sys create`**, not directly:
9	the command scans the workspace for the sibling components' scaffold records
10	(`.intropy/scaffold.json`), renders this template, and then its codegen
11	assembles the declaration on top. Rendering it directly (as the repo's example
12	fixtures do) produces a valid *empty* system.
13	
14	## Ownership split
15	
16	The renderer and the CLI's codegen own different files:
17	
18	| Owner | Files |
19	|---|---|
20	| this skeleton | `Program.cs`, `<Project>.SystemHost.csproj`, `Taskfile.yml`, `Properties/launchSettings.json`, `AGENTS.md`, `README.md`, `.gitignore` |
21	| this skeleton, as compilable placeholders that codegen overwrites | `<Project>System.cs`, `Topics.cs` |
22	| `intropy sys create` codegen only | `Apis.cs`, `Connectors.cs`, the sibling `<Project>.Contracts/` project |
23	
24	The host csproj's reference to `../<Project>.Contracts/` is `Exists`-guarded,
25	so a direct render builds before the Contracts project is generated.
26	
27	An empty system compiles, and `dotnet run -- check` reports **ITP002** ("a
28	system must declare at least one component") until `Define()` declares
29	components — for a fresh render that error is correct behavior.
30	
31	## Parameters
32	
33	| name | required | notes |
34	|---|---|---|

# system-host

The Aspire host project of an Intropy integration system: a .NET Aspire
AppHost whose one job is to hold the system's source of truth — a typed C#
declaration of which components exist and which topics connect them — and to
run, validate, or generate the system from that one declaration.

This template is normally rendered by **`intropy sys create`**, not directly:
the command scans the workspace for the sibling components' scaffold records
(`.intropy/scaffold.json`), renders this template, and then its codegen
assembles the declaration on top. Rendering it directly (as the repo's example
fixtures do) produces a valid *empty* system.

## Ownership split

The renderer and the CLI's codegen own different files:

| Owner | Files |
|---|---|
| this skeleton | `Program.cs`, `<Project>.SystemHost.csproj`, `Taskfile.yml`, `Properties/launchSettings.json`, `AGENTS.md`, `README.md`, `.gitignore` |
| this skeleton, as compilable placeholders that codegen overwrites | `<Project>System.cs`, `Topics.cs` |
| `intropy sys create` codegen only | `Apis.cs`, `Connectors.cs`, the sibling `<Project>.Contracts/` project |

The host csproj's reference to `../<Project>.Contracts/` is `Exists`-guarded,
so a direct render builds before the Contracts project is generated.

An empty system compiles, and `dotnet run -- check` reports **ITP002** ("a
system must declare at least one component") until `Define()` declares
components — for a fresh render that error is correct behavior.

## Parameters

| name | required | notes |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | yes | DNS-1123 system name, e.g. `order-flow`. Becomes `SystemName`. |

`sys create` renders with only `name` and `--no-input`, so no other parameter
may ever be required. The derived `projectName`/`systemClass` values
(`order-flow` → `OrderFlow` / `OrderFlowSystem`) must keep matching the CLI's
`pascalCase` derivation: codegen overwrites `<projectName>System.cs`, and a
disagreement would add a second `ISystemDefinition` beside the placeholder
instead of replacing it (discovery then fails at runtime).

## Rendering locally

```bash
intropy int create system-host -o /tmp/system-host-out \
  -f system-host/examples/minimal.yaml --version main --no-input
```

Building the render requires the `Intropy.Topology.Aspire` /
`Intropy.Topology.Generation` packages (0.1.0) to be resolvable from a NuGet
feed; until they are published, pack the Intropy.Topology repo to a local
folder feed.

content.text:
`intropy sys create` is implemented and verified end-to-end. All tests pass (`make check` and `-race`; `golangci-lint` isn't installed locally, so that one CI step is unverified).

## What landed in `intropy-cli` (branch `feature/system`)

- **Scaffold record prerequisite** — `int create` now records the templates' `intropy.dev/block-kind` and `data-flow` labels into `.intropy/scaffold.json` (`internal/template/scaffold.go`, both writer sites). The docs already claimed this happened; now it does.
- **`internal/system` package** — `Assemble` classifies workspace records (shared-library → contract project, extractor/loader → components, everything else skipped with a warning) and validates: duplicate component names, conflicting contracts per topic, zero components, zero/multiple shared libraries, and Topics.cs field-name collisions all produce specific errors naming the offending record paths. All local validation runs before any network I/O.
- **Codegen** — overwrites the template's `Topics.cs` and `<Name>System.cs` placeholders with the assembled declaration, guarded by a check that fails loudly if the template's `systemClass` derivation ever disagrees with the CLI (instead of silently creating a second `ISystemDefinition`). The CLI inserts the `ProjectReference` to the shared `Models/` project into the rendered csproj.
- **`sys` noun** — `intropy sys create -n OrderFlow [-o dir] [--version] [--force] [--output-json]`. `-n` accepts PascalCase or kebab (parity with sprig's `kebabcase` is locked by a test). Deliberately no `--set`/`--values`: the template contract is "only `name`, never prompt". README gained the noun and a Systems section.
- **Derivation-drift safety** — instead of reimplementing the template's PascalCase derivation in Go, `Create` reads `projectName`/`systemClass` back from the host's own just-written scaffold record, so CLI and template can't disagree.

## Companion changes in `intropy-templates` (uncommitted, separate repo)

Extractor/loader now declare `contract: 'Order'` and `pubsub: 'pubsub'` in `spec.values` (the topic→type join `sys create` needs); the system-host csproj lost its dead `<Name>.Contracts` Exists-guard; placeholders dropped their namespaces to match the tutorial's namespace-less output; README/CLAUDE.md updated to the "reference Models, don't generate Contracts" design. **Ordering matters:** these must be released before `sys create` works against `latest` — records scaffolded from today's released templates will error with guidance about the missing `contract` value.

## Verification

Beyond the unit suites, I ran a full tutorial replay against the real local templates checkout (extractor → loader → `sys create`): the generated `Topics.cs` and `OrderFlowSystem.cs` match chapter 3 byte-for-byte and the csproj gets `../Models/Models.csproj`. I removed that throwaway test since it depends on a sibling-repo path. One thing I couldn't verify here: `dotnet run -- check` on the assembled host needs the `Intropy.Topology.*` 0.1.0 packages on a NuGet feed — worth one manual replay once you have the local feed packed.

The shared-models skeleton hardcodes `Order.cs`/`OrderLine.cs` as sample content, and the extractor/loader sample logic compiles against that `Order` type. content.text: What would you like to clarify? I can expand on any of the options — e.g. exactly which files a neutral rename would touch, how the `empty=true` migration flow interacts with each choice, or what the tutorial diff would look like for the required-parameter route.

**Required parameter** — make `contract` a required parameter next to `topic`, no default.

The reasoning:

1. **It completes the declaration the tutorial already teaches.** Chapter 1's whole framing is "each scaffold declares its own half of the contract, and records it for the system to assemble." The contract is the topic *and* the type it carries — requiring the topic but silently injecting the type is half a declaration. `-s topic=orders -s contract=Order` reads as one coherent statement.

2. **The scaffold record must never lie, because `sys create` trusts it.** That's the real flaw with both a default and a neutral constant: in the `empty=true` migration flow (where a scaffold is created for, say, an Invoice integration), a defaulted `contract: Order` or `contract: EventModel` produces a record that's simply wrong, and `sys create` will faithfully generate `TopicRef<Order>` from it. A required parameter makes the recorded value always intentional. This is also the option most consistent with your "deterministic over complexity" principle — no hidden fallback to get out of sync.

3. **The neutral rename doesn't actually solve your objection.** `EventModel` is still a hardcoded name — just a vaguer one — and it makes the typed topic *less* useful (the point of `TopicRef<Order>` is documenting what flows). Plus it blands out the samples and forces a tutorial rewrite.

4. **The costs are small and honest.** Tutorial chapters 1–2 gain one flag per command. Interactive users who omit it get prompted (that machinery already exists). And the one awkward case — someone passes `contract=Invoice` while keeping the sample logic that compiles against `Order` — is exactly the "you own the refactor" situation you described; the parameter description can say so explicitly.

Concretely the change is: in `extractor/template.yaml` + `loader/template.yaml`, move `contract` from `spec.values` into required `parameters` (pattern `^[A-Z][A-Za-z0-9]*$`, description noting the sample contract is `Order` and that a different value means renaming the record in `Models/`), keep `pubsub: 'pubsub'` in `spec.values` as-is, and add `-s contract=Order` to the two scaffold commands in tutorial chapters 1–2. No CLI changes needed — it already reads `values.contract` and its "missing contract" error guidance stays accurate.

I'd skip parameterizing shared-models for now (option 4) — it only half-works while the sample pipeline code still references `Order`, and it can be layered on later without breaking anything.

lastPrompt: Should we rename the "Models" project "Contracts" instead while we are at it?

content.text:
Yes, I'd recommend it — with one caveat about ripple.

**Why it's the right rename:**

- **It completes the vocabulary you've already committed to.** The tutorial's narrative is "each scaffold declares its own half of the *contract*"; the new required parameter is literally named `contract`; the topology docs say the type parameter "is the contract the topic carries". A project named `Contracts/` closes the loop: contracts live in Contracts. "Models" is the vaguest name in .NET.
- **It resolves a real ambiguity the tutorial itself trips over.** Each integration keeps its *private* shapes in `src/Model/` (`In.cs`, `Out.cs`) while the *shared* types sit in `Models/` — Model vs Models as the private/shared distinction is one typo away from confusion. Model (private) vs Contracts (shared) is unambiguous.
- **It matches the .NET side.** The `OrderFulfillment` example in Intropy.Topology already uses a sibling `*.Contracts/` project, and the system-host csproj guard we just deleted also said Contracts. It's also the established convention in .NET messaging (MassTransit et al. literally call this project Contracts).
- **The CLI needs zero changes.** Everything keys off the `shared-library` role and `values.name` — the generated `using Models;` becomes `using Contracts;` automatically. Only fixture strings and a "typically `Models/`" in the README would want a cosmetic touch-up.

**The caveat — this is a templates + docs rename, and now is the last cheap moment:**

1. `extractor`/`loader` `template.yaml`: `models: 'Models'` → `'Contracts'` (the dependency output, ProjectReference paths, and scaffold record all follow, since they're templated off that value).
2. Skeleton source: wherever the sample code does `using Models;` — need to check whether that's templated off `{{ .models }}` or hardcoded; if hardcoded, a few `.cs.tmpl` edits.
3. Arguably rename the template directory `shared-models/` → `shared-contracts/` for coherence. That's the one breaking-ish bit: existing workspaces have records saying `template: shared-models`, and dependency idempotency matches on that name — a mixed workspace would get a new `Contracts/` next to the old `Models/`. Pre-release, I'd say acceptable; alternatively keep the directory name and live with "shared-models renders Contracts".
4. **The tutorial goes stale again** — ch. 1–3 mention `Models/` throughout (`using Models;` in the ch. 3 listing included). That pass is unavoidable if we rename, otherwise the docs actively contradict the scaffolds.

So: rename yes, and I'd do the template directory too while everything is pre-release. Want me to apply it (templates + CLI cosmetic strings), and do you want the tutorial pass included this time or left to you again?

1	# CLAUDE.md
2	
3	This file provides guidance to Claude Code when working in this repository.
4	
5	## What this repo is
6	
7	A library of **Intropy templates**. Each template is a scaffold
8	rendered into a working project by the `intropy` CLI (separate repo:
9	`integrio-intropy/intropy-cli`). The CLI is the only renderer; this repo
10	contains content, not code.
11	
12	The model is intentionally narrow: one engine (Go `text/template` + sprig),
13	one manifest format, one source of truth per template.
14	
15	## Repository layout
16	
17	```
18	<template>/
19	  template.yaml          # required: the intropy.dev/v1 manifest
20	  skeleton/              # required: rendered into the user's --output
21	    <files…>             # `.tmpl` files are templated; everything else is copied
22	  README.md              # optional: author-facing — what this template produces
23	  examples/              # optional: test fixtures for local renders
24	    minimal.yaml
25	    full.yaml
26	```
27	
28	Rules:
29	
30	- The CLI selects a template via positional argument:
31	  `intropy int create hello-world -o ./out`.
32	- Only `<template>/template.yaml` is parsed; only `<template>/skeleton/` is
33	  walked by the renderer.
34	- Anything else at the template root (README, examples, CHANGELOG, ADRs) is
35	  invisible to the renderer — it's for the template author, not the
36	  scaffolded project.
37	- There is **no shared content between templates**. No repo-level
38	  `skeletons/` dir, no cross-template includes. If two templates need the
39	  same file, duplicate it. (Composition happens at the *output* level:
40	  a template may declare whole sibling templates under `spec.dependencies`
41	  — see below — but never share skeleton files with them.)
42	
43	## Manifest schema (`<template>/template.yaml`)
44	
45	```yaml
46	apiVersion: intropy.dev/v1
47	kind: Template
48	metadata:
49	  name: <kebab-case>           # convention: match the directory name
50	  title: <Title Case>
51	  description: <one sentence>
52	  tags: [example, go, http]
53	  labels:                      # two intropy.dev/* keys are load-bearing (see below)
54	    intropy.io/template-level: example
55	    intropy.dev/block-kind: extractor   # extractor | loader | aggregator | transactional-integration
56	    intropy.dev/data-flow: "in"         # in | out | both | internal
57	spec:
58	  parameters:                  # raw JSON Schema; type must be "object"
59	    type: object
60	    required: [name]
61	    properties:
62	      name:
63	        type: string
64	        title: Service name
65	        description: Lowercase kebab-case identifier.
66	        pattern: "^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$"
67	      port:
68	        type: integer
69	        default: 8080
70	  values:                      # optional; derived values rendered via Go template + sprig
71	    module: 'github.com/example/{{ .name }}'
72	  dependencies:                # optional; sibling templates scaffolded when missing
73	    - template: shared-contracts  # directory name in this repo
74	      output: '{{ .contracts }}'  # Go template; single path segment (conventionally "Models")
75	      values:                  # Go templates over this template's resolved values
76	        name: '{{ .contracts }}'
77	```
78	
79	Notes:
80	
81	- **`spec.parameters` is plain JSON Schema.** Types: `string`, `boolean`,
82	  `integer`, `number`. Supported attributes: `title`, `description`, `pattern`,
83	  `enum`, `default`. The same schema validates CLI inputs and drives the
84	  Backstage form when a Template entity references this template.
85	- **Parameter declaration order matters** for human display. Keep the YAML
86	  order intentional.
87	- **`spec.values` derives string values from parameters.** Each entry is a Go
88	  template (with sprig) rendered against the resolved parameters. Use for
89	  composite values needed in multiple skeleton files (e.g. a module path).
90	  Output is always a string. Don't chain entries — map iteration order
91	  is non-deterministic.
92	- **Two labels are load-bearing.** The CLI reads `intropy.dev/block-kind`
93	  (`extractor` | `loader` | `aggregator` | `transactional-integration`) and
94	  `intropy.dev/data-flow` (`in` | `out` | `both` | `internal`) at render time
95	  and records them in the scaffolded project's `.intropy/scaffold.json`, which
96	  `intropy sys create` later assembles into the system declaration. Templates
97	  that are a system block must declare both. Everything else under `labels`
98	  is free-form.
99	- **`spec.dependencies` composes whole templates at the output level.** Each
100	  entry names a sibling template in this repo, an `output` (a Go template
101	  that must render to a single path segment — the dependency is created as a
102	  direct sibling of the component's output directory), and a `values` map
103	  (Go templates rendered against the declaring template's resolved values).
104	  The CLI renders dependencies from the same fetched tag right after the
105	  component render. Idempotency: a target directory whose
106	  `.intropy/scaffold.json` names the same template is **skipped silently**
107	  (drift in values only warns); a missing or empty directory is rendered; a
108	  foreign scaffold record or an unmanaged non-empty directory is an error.
109	  `--force` never propagates to dependencies. The component's scaffold
110	  record lists every declared dependency under `dependsOn`.
111	  Authoring rules:
112	  - A dependency render never prompts — the `values` map plus the dependency
113	    template's own defaults must cover all its required parameters.
114	  - Shared-support templates (like `shared-contracts`) declare
115	    `intropy.dev/template-role: shared-library` and **no**
116	    `intropy.dev/block-kind` / `data-flow` labels; the role is recorded in
117	    scaffold.json so system assembly can tell them apart from blocks.
118	  - A skeleton may reference its declared dependencies (e.g. a
119	    `ProjectReference` to `../../<dep>/…`) — the mechanism guarantees the
120	    sibling exists. The system-host skeleton never references the workspace's
121	    shared contracts project; `intropy sys create` discovers it by its
122	    scaffold record and inserts that reference itself.
123	- **No `spec.steps`**, no `spec.owner`, no `nextSteps`. The model is
124	  intentionally narrow: a manifest declares parameters and the skeleton tree
125	  describes what gets written.
126	
127	## Skeleton conventions (`<template>/skeleton/`)
128	
129	- **File contents are templated only if the filename ends in `.tmpl`.** The
130	  `.tmpl` suffix is stripped on output (`README.md.tmpl` → `README.md`).
131	- **Filenames and directory names are templated** with the same `{{ .param }}`
132	  syntax as file contents (e.g. `src/{{ .name }}.csproj`). The `.tmpl` suffix
133	  only governs whether *file contents* are rendered; path segments are always
134	  templated.
135	- **Use `{{ .paramName }}` to reference parameters and derived values.** The
136	  data context is a flat map containing parameters + `spec.values` entries.
137	- **Sprig is available.** `upper`, `lower`, `title`, `kebabcase`,
138	  `snakecase`, `replace`, `default`, `trim`, `len`, `get`, `dict`. Full list:
139	  https://masterminds.github.io/sprig/ .
140	- **Missing keys are a hard error.** The renderer runs with
141	  `missingkey=error`. Typos like `{{ .Name }}` (wrong case) fail the render
142	  with a clear message — they don't silently produce empty strings.
143	- **Sprig functions with side effects exist** (`env`, `now`, `uuidv4`,
144	  `getHostByName`). Don't use them — they break the "same inputs → same
145	  output" reproducibility guarantee.
146	
147	Example skeleton file `skeleton/README.md.tmpl`:
148	
149	```markdown
150	# {{ .name }}
151	
152	Generated from the `{{ .name }}` template.
153	
154	Module: `{{ .module }}`
155	```

158	
159	Every skeleton ships an `AGENTS.md.tmpl` at its root. `AGENTS.md` (per the
160	[agents.md](https://agents.md/) standard, auto-loaded by most coding agents)
161	is the scaffolded project's **manifest for agents**: the facts about *this*

# 1. The extractor

In this chapter you create the system workspace, scaffold the first of its two integrations, and run it alone: a complete integration on its own isolated components, before any system exists.

## Scaffold

Create the workspace and render the `extractor` blueprint into it:

```bash
mkdir order-flow && cd order-flow
intropy int create extractor -n OrderExtractor -s organization=Fluxia -s topic=orders -o order-extractor
```

`order-flow/` is the system workspace: a plain directory that holds the two integrations and, from chapter 3, the SystemHost as siblings. Nothing about it is special. Each integration stays an independent project you could version, test, and deploy on its own.

Two flags deserve a closer look:

- **`-s topic=orders`:** the pub/sub topic the extractor publishes to. You'll type the same value when scaffolding the loader — each scaffold declares its own half of the contract, and records it (in `.intropy/scaffold.json`) for the system to assemble in chapter 3.
- **No `empty=true`:** unlike the transactional tutorial, you keep the blueprint's sample logic. This tutorial is about what happens between integrations, so the insides stay stock.

The render's last line reports a project you didn't ask for: `created dependency Contracts from template shared-contracts`. The workspace now holds two directories:

```
order-flow/
├── Contracts/                       # shared contract types — scaffolded once per workspace
│   ├── Contracts.csproj
│   ├── Order.cs                  # the order contract the extractor publishes
│   └── OrderLine.cs
└── order-extractor/
    ├── Taskfile.yml              # task run / build / test
    ├── docker-compose.yml        # local observability stack — standalone runs only
    ├── local/
    │   ├── dapr-components/
    │   │   ├── poll.yaml         # cron binding — sweeps the inbound folder every 5 s
    │   │   ├── inbound.yaml      # folder binding — stands in for the source system
    │   │   └── pubsub.yaml       # in-memory pub/sub, component name "pubsub"
    │   └── sample-data/
    │       └── sample-order.json
    ├── src/                      # implemented: sweep inbound, transform, publish
    └── test/
```

The extractor itself looks like the transactional layout you know, with its own components. `Contracts/` is new: the extractor template declares the `shared-contracts` template as a dependency, so scaffolding the first block into a workspace also scaffolds the workspace's contract library next to it. It holds the `Order` record (and its `OrderLine` lines): the shape the extractor publishes, defined in neither block because both halves of the system need it. The extractor references it as an ordinary `ProjectReference` (`../../Contracts/Contracts.csproj`); its own source shape stays private in `src/Model/In.cs`, and the pipeline's transform step maps that `In` to the shared `Order` before publishing.

The sample logic ships working. On every poll tick it lists the inbound folder, publishes each file's content as an `Order` message on topic `orders`, and deletes the source file. And unlike the transactional integration, which runs once and exits, the extractor keeps running until you stop it — that matters in chapter 5, when you'll drop files in while the whole system is live.

## Check it

Run the extractor standalone:

```bash
cd order-extractor
task run
```

The task seeds `sample-order.json` into the inbound folder and starts the integration under Dapr, with the sidecar loading only `local/dapr-components/`. Within a poll tick you should see:

```
== APP == info: OrderExtractor.Pipeline[0]
== APP ==       Swept 1 file from inbound
== APP == info: OrderExtractor.Pipeline[0]
== APP ==       Published ORD-1001 to topic orders (pubsub)
```

Stop it with Ctrl+C, then confirm the source file is gone:

```bash
ls local/storage/inbound/
```

The folder is empty: the extractor swept the file, published it, and cleaned up.

Where did the message go? Into the extractor's own in-memory pub/sub — and nothing subscribes there. That's the point of an isolated run: it verifies the extractor's whole job (sweep, publish, clean up) without needing a consumer to exist. Delivery to a consumer is the system's job, and that's chapter 5.

!!! check "Recap"
    - Created the `order-flow` workspace; integrations and the SystemHost live in it as siblings
    - Scaffolded `order-extractor` from the `extractor` blueprint with its sample logic intact
    - The render also scaffolded `Contracts/`, the workspace's shared contract library — the `Order` record the extractor publishes lives there, not in the extractor
    - Standalone, the sidecar loads only `local/dapr-components/`: an isolated, in-memory world
    - The published message intentionally went nowhere — no consumer exists yet
